tools.name: reference
tools.description:
The rule book (book="rules", the default) or the playbook (book="playbook": how_to_play's topics, `section`
the topic). The rule book, as Markdown: what every unit, building, wonder, project, process, promotion, social
policy and ideology tenet, technology, belief, resource, terrain, feature, improvement, specialist and
unit action does, read once from this game's own database (mods and DLC included) and cached. No other
answer repeats this text (since runtime v216): chooser rows carry the enum, the name and live numbers,
and a resource tile carries its resource name. Sections, one per call with `section`: terrain,
resources, improvements, units, buildings, projects, processes, promotions, policies, techs, beliefs,
specialists, actions. The whole book is long (tens of thousands of tokens): read it once at the start of
a game if you can hold it, otherwise the section a choice needs. Also served as the MCP resources
civ5://reference and civ5://reference/{section}. Usable while it is not
my turn.

section.description: one section: a rule-book heading (terrain, units, buildings, ...) or a playbook topic; left out, the book's index
section.title: Section

book.description: 'rules' (default): what everything in this game does; 'playbook': how to play through these tools
book.title: Book

annotations.title: The rule book and the playbook

tools.name: turn
tools.description: The clock. action: status (whose turn, the gate, what blocks ending it; today's turn_status), briefing (my turn in one read: decisions with their `actions` rows, changes, board, threats, notes; since='turn' after a context reset, detail='digest' for the event digest alone), finish (run `actions` rows, end the turn, wait until it is mine again and return the new turn; notes='new' / 'all' picks which notebook notes ride on the reply; `timeout_seconds`), end (end the turn only), wait (block until it is my turn). Other arguments of the old call by name in `args` (finish_turn's skip_quiet_turns, wake_on, autosave, briefing). Returns the turn: turn, my_turn, `gate` (null, or what must be answered first), todo / decisions, digest, notes; finish and wait return once it is my turn again or the timeout passes (then with my_turn false, nothing lost).

actions.description: finish only: order rows to run before the turn ends, [{tool, args}] as the reads hand them back
actions.title: Actions

since.description: briefing: 'previous' (default) compares with my last briefing, 'turn' with the last turn end (after a context reset)
since.title: Since

limit.description: briefing: rows per list of changes and notes (default 8)
limit.title: Limit

notes.description: finish: which notebook notes ride on the reply, 'new' (default) or 'all'
notes.title: Notes

timeout_seconds.description: finish / wait: seconds to wait for my turn before answering with the state so far (default 600)
timeout_seconds.title: Timeout Seconds

args.description: other arguments of the old call by name: skip_quiet_turns, wake_on, autosave, briefing
args.title: Args

tools.name: inspect
tools.description:
A read of the world: `what` names the object, `view` the part of it (the default view when left out); `id` the one object (a unit, city, civ, city-state or spy id; a list for units/actions). Every reply that lists what can be done carries `actions` / `call` rows for order. what: views --
  empire: default, demographics
  notifications: default
  screen: tech_tree, religion, culture, culture_works, great_people, domination, spaceship, wonders, intrigue, trade_routes, deals
  league: default
  spies: default
  units: default, actions
  unit: actions, targets, tactical, home
  cities: default
  city: screen, production, strikes
  map: window, grid, index, frontier
  civs: default
  civ: summary, war, trade_catalog
  city_state: summary, full
  options: research, policies, beliefs, trade_routes, spy_cities
  compare: default
Selectors: x, y, radius (map/window, unit/tactical), mission (unit/targets), kind (options/beliefs, compare), detail, since, limit, item + yield_type (city/production prices one item), `args` for the rest by the old name (compare's fields). Replies are the old reads' replies unchanged.

what.description: the object: empire, notifications, screen, league, spies, units, unit, cities, city, map, civs, civ, city_state, options, compare
what.title: What

id.description: the one object's id (unit, city, civ, city-state or spy); a list of unit ids for units/actions
id.title: Id

view.description: the part of the object, from the list below; the default view when left out
view.title: View

x.description: map/window centre or unit/tactical origin, with y
x.title: X

radius.description: map/window, unit/tactical: tiles around x, y
radius.title: Radius

mission.description: unit/targets: the mission whose legal targets to list
mission.title: Mission

kind.description: options/beliefs: the belief kind; compare: what to compare
kind.title: Kind

detail.description: 'summary' or 'full' where a view offers both
detail.title: Detail

since.description: notifications: only those after this turn
since.title: Since

limit.description: how many rows a list returns
limit.title: Limit

yield_type.description: city/production with item: the yield to price it in
yield_type.title: Yield Type

args.description: the rest by the old call's name (compare's fields)
args.title: Args

tools.name: order
tools.description:
An order to something I own: `to` the target kind, `id` which one, `action` the verb, `args` its arguments by name (a refusal names the shape with an example). to: actions --
  unit: move, mission, promote, upgrade, disband, trade_route, plunder
  city: produce, purchase, dequeue, sell_building, buy_plot, specialist, work_plot, governor, status, strike, great_work
  empire: research, policy, ideology, switch_ideology, pantheon, religion, enhance_religion, reformation, faith_purchase
  civ: propose_deal, negotiate, peace, demand, friendship, declare_war, denounce, event
  city_state: gift_gold, gift_unit, gift_improvement (or a city-state screen button by its name: pledge, revoke_pledge, bully_gold, bully_unit, declare_war, make_peace)
  league: propose, repeal, vote
  spy: move, coup
Copy the rows a read hands back (`actions`, `call`) as they are; `action_id` replays a retried order. Returns {ok: true, ...} with what changed (a unit's new plot, a city's queue, a deal's answer), or {ok: false, err, choices / accepts, example} naming why and the legal shape; nothing is acted on when ok is false. Orders change the game and most cannot be undone (disband, declare_war, a purchase).

to.description: the target kind, something I own
to.title: To

action.description: the verb; its words depend on `to` (oneOf below)
action.title: Action

id.description: which unit, city, civ, city-state or spy; empire and league take none
id.title: Id

args.description: the action's arguments by name, as the copied row has them; a refusal shows the shape with an example
args.title: Args

action_id.description: a token of my choosing: a retry with the same action_id replays the stored result instead of acting twice
action_id.title: Action Id

action.description: gift_gold, gift_unit, gift_improvement, or a city-state screen button by its name (pledge, revoke_pledge, bully_gold, bully_unit, declare_war, make_peace)

tools.name: question
tools.description: What the game is asking right now, with its `answers` rows: the decision popup's choices (a tech, a production item, a policy, a promotion, a belief, a ruins reward, a captured city's fate, a Great Person, a dig), the leader on screen and the deal on the table (the buttons), or nothing pending (then the turn's open decisions). `gate` rides on the reply. answer() takes the choice.

tools.name: answer
tools.description: Answer what the game is asking: `choice` is the item's name (a TECH_, UNIT_, BUILDING_, POLICY_, PROMOTION_, BELIEF_ or goody name; liberate / annex / puppet / raze; a dig's choice number), a popup's or leader screen's button number, or on a leader screen accept / refuse (a deal on the table), leave (close it), accept_friendship. `args` carries the rest the popup needs (a promotion's unit_id, a dig's x and y, a stolen tech's player_id, a religion's beliefs and city). Dispatches on the gate: question() shows which question is up. Returns {ok, ...} with the popup's outcome and the gate that follows (still_pending and `next` when another leader waits), or {ok: false, err, choices}.

choice.description: the `answers` row's choice: an item name, a button number, or accept / refuse / leave / accept_friendship
choice.title: Choice

args.description: what the popup needs beyond the choice: unit_id, x and y, player_id, beliefs, city
args.title: Args

action_id.description: a token of my choosing: a retry with the same action_id replays the stored result
action_id.title: Action Id

tools.name: notebook
tools.description: My memory, kept beside the game per seat and surviving a context reset: free-text notes, assignments (what a unit or city is for) and multi-turn orders for units. Use it for what future-me must know; the game itself holds no plan. action, with its args -- remember {text, tag?, replace_id?}: write a note (returns the note with its id; new notes ride on the next briefing / finish); recall {tag?, limit?}: list notes; forget {note_id}: delete a note for good. assign {role, purpose, unit_ids? / city_ids?}: give units or cities a purpose that shows in their rows; assignments: list them; amend {assignment_id, purpose? / role?}; close {assignment_id}. give_order {unit_id, steps}: a plan of steps run one per turn at each finish; orders: the plans with their status; cancel_order / resume_order {order_id}. Returns {ok: true, ...} with the row written or the rows listed, or {ok: false, err, accepts, example}. A note written on a turn later than the one on screen (a save was loaded) comes back marked later_timeline.

action.description: remember | recall | forget | assign | assignments | amend | close | give_order | orders | cancel_order | resume_order
action.title: Action

args.description: the action's arguments by name: text / tag / replace_id, note_id, role and purpose with unit_ids / city_ids, assignment_id, unit_id and steps, order_id
args.title: Args

action_id.description: a token of my choosing: a retry with the same action_id replays the stored result
action_id.title: Action Id

tools.name: batch
tools.description: Many orders in one call, in order: actions is a list of {tool, args} rows -- the rows every read hands back, old or new names alike -- each answered under `results`; the first refusal stops the rest (stop_on_refusal=false runs them all). Not inside: the turn's wait / finish / end, a load, the seat, the exit, a batch. turn(action='finish', actions=[...]) runs a batch and ends the turn in one call. Returns {ok, results: [one reply per row], stopped_at?}; the rows act on the game as the orders they carry.

actions.description: the rows to run in order, [{tool, args}], as every read hands them back
actions.title: Actions

stop_on_refusal.description: stop at the first refused row (default true); false runs them all
stop_on_refusal.title: Stop On Refusal

force.description: take over this turn's claim held by another client of my seat
force.title: Force

tools.name: session
tools.description: Saves, loads and the seat of this game session: keep a state before a risky turn, open another save, leave a finished game. It never plays a turn. action -- save: a quick save of the game on screen (returns the save written); load {filename}: open that save in the live game, replacing the unsaved state on screen (save first); load_latest: open the newest save, whichever game it is; main_menu: leave the game for the main menu (the game_over gate's way out); seat {seat}: which human seat this server plays in a hotseat game (a server pinned with --seat refuses a change onto the other human seat; never move onto the seat on screen). Returns {ok: true, turn, seat, ...} or {ok: false, err} with the legal filenames or seats. In a game with other people ask the human before loading.

args.description: load: {filename} (a save's name without the single/ prefix); seat: {seat} (0 or 1)
args.title: Args
